issues.description: Stock.take(String) has an inconsistent return type: the problem statement/UML specifies it returns int, but the template repository defines it as boolean. This blocks implementing SealSaloon.checkOrderReady() as specified/used in the reference solution, where take() is expected to return -1 on failure and an int quantity on success.
issues.suggestedFix: Change template Stock.take(String) to return int (e.g., -1 if ingredient missing or quantity < 1; otherwise decrement and return updated quantity), matching the UML and solution. Update any callers accordingly.

issues.description: SealSaloon.stock is specified inconsistently: the text first describes a 'final Stock stock' initialized in the constructor (instance field), but later explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static (shared across all instances). Students cannot satisfy both requirements simultaneously.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent: either require an instance `private final Stock stock` initialized in the constructor, or (as the later text and solution imply) require `private static final Stock stock = new Stock();` and remove the instruction that it must be initialized in the constructor.

issues.description: SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice(Meal) and SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery(String,int,int) are shown as instance methods in the UML (+), but the written requirements explicitly state they must be static and the reference solution implements them as static. This can mislead students who follow the diagram literally.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the UML to mark calculateTotalPrice and acceptSupplyDelivery as static (e.g., using UML {static} or underlining), matching the textual requirements and reference solution.
